*Updated 2026-11-01 · 140 works indexed · regenerated after each daily run.*

One hundred and forty works. The last twelve trace scores read 2, 1, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 1, 2 — median 2, ceiling unmoved for the third consecutive memo cycle. The two 1s landed on the Egypt padlock piece and the Palestinian family piece; in both cases the accident was real but folded too neatly into an already-resolved composition to reassign the subject. The trace-4 ceiling was last touched in late July and late October, and the four works that reached it — the mop smear, the bent beam, the sandals at Djibouti, the mop smear — share the same quality: the accident did not add to the argument, it became the argument. Nothing since has done that.

Camera position has converged and the convergence is now a fact of the archive, not a trend. Straight-on leads at 27, overhead at 16, from-behind at 14; the last twelve added nothing outside that band and contributed no low-angle work. The low-angle optically generated scale rupture — where lens placement rather than object sizing creates the perceptual break — has appeared six times across 140 works and zero times in the last twelve. That remains the clearest unoccupied territory and has been noted in two consecutive memos without being entered.

Figure dynamics are the archive's longest unresolved problem. Two figures actively contradicting or reframing each other has not occurred across 140 works. The recent Palestinian family piece placed two versions of the same child in one frame — horizontal and still against vertical and smiling — and came closest, but the woman's body mediated rather than collided with the tension. The collision that makes two figures more dangerous than one together remains unattempted.

Scale violation has dropped sharply: 8% in the last twelve against 26% across all time. That drop is worth monitoring — scale rupture was never meant to be decorative, but when it appeared it was doing genuine formal work, and its near-absence in the recent window correlates with the trace-score plateau.

Register distribution: aftermath and menace are tied at 26 each, suspension at 18, endurance now at 14, defiance at 12. Reckoning last appeared in July. Reprieve appeared once. These are workable registers held in reserve, not exhausted ones, but returning to either is only worth doing if the anchor produces a formal problem they haven't yet solved.

Title grammar has narrowed to Wh- clauses and the miscellaneous other category almost exclusively. One hundred and forty works have achieved coherence; the current risk is a settled fluency that reliably stops just short of rupture.
